## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Points
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Cartesian and homogeneous points
//  - Curvilinear coordinates
//  - Parametric coordinates

//==
// # Cartesian and homogeneous points
//
// Points are positions in a space (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point_(geometry));
// they are not vectors. Subtracting two points yields a vector, and adding a
// vector to a point yields a point (the IDifference interface). This section holds
// the Cartesian positions and their homogeneous (projective) form; the
// curvilinear systems and the parametric weightings follow below.

// A position in the 2D Cartesian plane
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartesian_coordinate_system).
type Point2D
    implements ICoordinate, IOriginBased<Vector2D>, IHashable, IMetricSpace, ITransformable2D
{
    X: Number;
    Y: Number;
}

// A position in 3D Cartesian space.
type Point3D
    implements ICoordinate, IOriginBased<Vector3D>, IHashable, IMetricSpace, ITransformable3D
{
    X: Number;
    Y: Number;
    Z: Number;
}

// A position in N-dimensional Cartesian space.
type PointN
    implements ICoordinate, IOriginBased<VectorN>, IMetricSpace
{
    Components: Array<Number>;
}

// A 2D point in homogeneous form; the Cartesian point is (X/W, Y/W)
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homogeneous_coordinates).
type HomogeneousPoint2D
    implements IValue
{
    X: Number;
    Y: Number;
    W: Number;
}

// A 3D point in homogeneous form; the Cartesian point is (X/W, Y/W, Z/W)
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homogeneous_coordinates).
type HomogeneousPoint3D
    implements IValue
{
    X: Number;
    Y: Number;
    Z: Number;
    W: Number;
}

//==
// # Curvilinear coordinates
//
// Positions expressed as radii and angles rather than Cartesian components
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curvilinear_coordinates). Each alternative
// coordinate system is a distinct type, not a convention layered over
// `Point2D`/`Point3D`, so a polar pair can never be mistaken for a Cartesian one.
// Angles are the `Angle` type throughout (see CONVENTIONS.md - Angles).

// A planar position as distance from origin and angle from the positive X axis
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polar_coordinate_system).
type PolarCoordinate
    implements IValue
{
    Radius: Number;
    Angle: Angle;
}

// A 3D position as planar polar coordinates plus height along Z
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cylindrical_coordinate_system).
type CylindricalCoordinate
    implements IValue
{
    Radius: Number;
    Azimuth: Angle;
    Height: Number;
}

// A 3D position as radius, azimuth (about Z from +X), and inclination from the
// +Z pole (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spherical_coordinate_system).
type SphericalCoordinate
    implements IValue
{
    Radius: Number;
    Azimuth: Angle;
    Inclination: Angle;
}

// A position on a planet's surface: geodetic latitude, longitude, and altitude
// above the reference ellipsoid
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geographic_coordinate_system).
type GeoCoordinate
    implements IValue
{
    Latitude: Angle;
    Longitude: Angle;
    Altitude: Length;
}

//==
// # Parametric coordinates
//
// Positions given relative to a host element rather than to world space: weights
// on a triangle's vertices, and normalized parameters on a surface or volume.
// Their meaning is only defined together with the element they parameterize, so
// they are kept as distinct types from the Cartesian points above.

// Weights relative to a triangle's vertices. Vertex binding: U -> the first
// vertex (A), V -> the second (B), W -> the third (C), so the point recovered on
// the triangle's support plane is U*A + V*B + W*C (see `Evaluate` in
// numeric-structures.library.plato).
// See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barycentric_coordinate_system.
//
// Invariant: U + V + W = 1 identifies a point on the support plane (an affine
// combination). Off-plane or non-normalized triples (U + V + W != 1) are
// degenerate for triangle evaluation; `IsNormalized` tests the sum against a
// tolerance. The three fields are kept deliberately (a two-component (V, W) form
// with U = 1 - V - W was rejected): the redundant U reads directly, and the
// invariant is documented rather than enforced by shape.
//
// Affine vs convex: U + V + W = 1 alone is an *affine* combination and
// may place the point anywhere on the plane; the point lies *inside* the
// triangle (a *convex* combination) exactly when additionally U, V, W >= 0.
type BarycentricCoordinate
    implements IValue
{
    U: Number;
    V: Number;
    W: Number;
}

// A normalized 2D surface parameter: texture lookup, patch evaluation
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UV_mapping).
// Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - UV origin (origin top-left, U right, V down).
type UvCoordinate
    implements ICoordinate, IOriginBased<Vector2D>
{
    U: Number;
    V: Number;
}
```
